text: An employee gets an email claiming to be from IT, asking them to verify their password at a link. Instead of clicking it, they forward it to the security team's phishing-report mailbox. That one forwarded email is the trigger for everything that follows -- a complete, realistic walk through a SOAR playbook from start to finish.

The moment the email lands in the mailbox, the SOAR platform picks it up as a new case -- ingest, made possible by orchestration connecting the platform to the mailbox's API. Extract pulls the sender address, the link, and any attachments automatically, the same work an analyst would otherwise do by hand. Enrich checks that sender and URL against threat intel feeds for outside context before anything gets decided.

Say the link resolves to a domain threat intel already flags as a known credential-harvesting site, registered three days ago -- a strong, specific signal, not a guess. On a confirmed-malicious verdict, the playbook quarantines the email from every inbox it reached, not just the reporter's, blocks the domain at the email gateway so future copies never arrive, and opens a case. On an inconclusive verdict, it routes straight to an analyst's queue instead.

Notice the analyst is told something on both branches, not only the one requiring judgment. On the confirmed branch there's no decision left to make, but an analyst still needs a visible record -- in case this is the fifth nearly-identical report this week, worth investigating as its own campaign. That's the force-multiplier relationship from the last lesson, in practice.

This single scenario uses every piece from this chapter: orchestration connects the mailbox, threat intel feed, and email gateway into one flow; automation runs the extraction and enrichment with nobody opening the email by hand; response actually quarantines and blocks instead of just alerting; and it qualifies for a playbook at all because it's repeatable and well-understood.

That's a full SOAR playbook, end to end, and it closes out this chapter's look at orchestration, automation, and response. Next, the chapter capstone puts you on the other side of the queue -- triaging a set of real-looking alerts yourself, using the triage process, correlation thinking, and now this SOAR context all together.
